zones.name: Drawbar & Front
zones.description: Lunette, brake actuator, and front support leg

steps.procedure: Check the lunette for secure mounting or obvious damage. (TM lists no "Not Fully Mission Capable" criterion for this item; report damage to Unit maintenance.)

(a) Inspect the area where the front roller pin goes through the brake actuator housing for damage and abnormal wear. (b) Inspect the master pin through the middle rear of the actuator for wear or damage. (c) Ensure the mounting nuts and bolts securely fasten the brake actuator assembly to the drawbar. (d) Visually check the breakaway cable and breakaway lever for damage and missing parts. Check that the breakaway lever is in the DOWN position.
steps.noGoCondition: a./b. Damage is evident. c. Nuts and bolts missing or damaged. d. Breakaway cable or lever is missing or damaged.

steps.procedure: WARNING: loaded tongue weight is up to 420 lb (190.5 kg) — use the support leg crank to raise and lower the drawbar; if the leg is inoperative, unload the trailer or use four or more people to lift the drawbar. Check the front support leg for damage, missing parts, and proper operation. Check that the caster moves freely and the handle can be cranked up and down to raise and lower the trailer. (TM lists no "Not Fully Mission Capable" criterion for this item; report faults to Unit maintenance.)
Check the left handbrake lever for damage or missing parts. Check that the handle can be engaged (lever LOWERED) and released (lever RAISED). Adjust as necessary (para 2-14).
steps.noGoCondition: Damage is evident or handbrake fails to operate correctly.

steps.procedure: Visually check the left tire for underinflation and unserviceability. Check for leaks, cuts, gouges, cracks, and bulges. Remove all penetrating objects. Correct pressure is 17 psi ± 2 psi (117 ± 13.8 kPa) (para 1-11).
steps.noGoCondition: Any tire is missing or unserviceable. Tires have leaks, cuts, gouges, cracks, or bulges which would result in tire failure during operation.

steps.procedure: Visually check the right tire for underinflation and unserviceability. Check for leaks, cuts, gouges, cracks, and bulges. Remove all penetrating objects. Correct pressure is 17 psi ± 2 psi (117 ± 13.8 kPa) (para 1-11).
steps.noGoCondition: Any tire is missing or unserviceable. Tires have leaks, cuts, gouges, cracks, or bulges which would result in tire failure during operation.

steps.procedure: Check the right handbrake lever for damage or missing parts. Check that the handle can be engaged (lever LOWERED) and released (lever RAISED). Adjust as necessary (para 2-14).
steps.noGoCondition: Damage is evident or handbrake fails to operate correctly.

steps.procedure: Connect the intervehicular cable to the towing vehicle (para 2-10). Operate the towing vehicle light switch through all settings and check the trailer lights.
steps.noGoCondition: Trailer lights do not operate properly.

zones.name: Rear & Underside
zones.description: Post-operation checks: stabilizers, shock absorbers, safety chains

steps.procedure: Inspect the rear stabilizers for damage. Ensure the hinge on the flex plate can be rotated and the sections slide up and down when the pin is removed.
steps.noGoCondition: Damage is evident or parts are missing.

steps.procedure: Inspect the shock absorbers for leaks, missing nuts, and damage.
steps.noGoCondition: Any leaks are evident, mounting hardware missing, damage is evident.

steps.procedure: Inspect the safety chains for damage or missing parts.
steps.noGoCondition: Damage is evident or parts are missing.

zones.name: Weekly Checks
zones.description: Wheel assemblies, brake lines, lights, cargo body, soft top, and frame

steps.procedure: Check the left wheel lugnuts and stud nuts to make sure they are not loose or missing. If any are loose, tighten.
steps.noGoCondition: Three or more lugnuts or stud nuts are missing.

steps.procedure: Inspect brake lines and hoses for missing clamps, cracks, leaks, loose connections, or broken lines. Tighten loose connections. (Any brake fluid leakage must be corrected — para 2-6.)

(a) Visually inspect lights and reflectors for missing or broken parts and loose connectors; tighten any loose connectors. (b) Inspect the wiring harness and intervehicular cable for exposed, frayed, or damaged wiring or missing mounting hardware. (Operating with damaged or inoperable trailer lights may violate AR 385-55.)
Check the right wheel lugnuts and stud nuts to make sure they are not loose or missing. If any are loose, tighten.
steps.noGoCondition: Three or more lugnuts or stud nuts are missing.

steps.procedure: (a) Inspect the cargo body for missing rivets, missing cargo tiedowns, and damage to the box. (b) Inspect the tailgate for damage, missing or broken hardware, missing or broken lanyard cable, and missing or damaged pin; check that the tailgate rotates freely on its hinges. (c) Inspect the decontamination bracket for damaged or missing hardware. (d) Check that the identification plate and shipping plate are firmly attached and readable. (e) Inspect the bows for damage.
Visually inspect the canvas cover for rips, tears, or missing footman loops.
Inspect the frame side rails for cracks, breaks, bends, wear, deterioration, and missing or loose fasteners.
steps.noGoCondition: Cracks, bends, or breaks in frame are present.

zones.name: Monthly Checks
zones.description: Brake master cylinder fluid level and condition

steps.procedure: Inspect the master cylinder assembly for a damaged or missing cap, leaks, and proper fluid level. If the cap is damaged or missing, replace it. Proper fluid level is 1/8 in. (3 mm) below the top edge of the reservoir; if not at that level, add fluid (Appendix G).
